tips.title: Fixing Silvered Decals After They Have Dried
tips.text: Silvered decals (visible silver film around markings) happen when air is trapped under the decal. To fix after drying: apply Mr. Mark Softer generously over the decal, wait 10 minutes, then press gently with a damp cotton swab from the center outward to force air bubbles out. Repeat twice more with fresh solution. If silvering persists, carefully slit the decal film with a fresh hobby knife blade in a crosshatch pattern, apply setting solution again, and press flat. Once fully settled, seal with a gloss coat. For stubborn cases, replace the decal and reapply with stronger solutions like Daco Strong.

tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kit Parts
tips.text: To remove old paint from kit parts, first soften the paint with Goo Gone or similar citrus-based cleaner. Apply with a cotton swab, let sit for 15 minutes, then gently scrape off with a dental pick or wooden toothpick. For stubborn areas, use a hobby knife to carefully scrape paint off in small sections. Wipe clean with a damp cloth, then allow parts to dry completely before priming.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Broken photo-etch parts can be repaired using CA glue (super glue). Apply a small drop of CA glue on a wooden toothpick, then gently apply it to the broken edge, allowing the glue to wick into the gap. Hold the parts together for 10-15 seconds until set. Once dry, gently sand any excess glue with fine grit sandpaper. For better adhesion, roughen the surface with a light scratch using a hobby knife or scribing tool before applying CA glue.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: Clogged airbrushes can be recovered using Vallejo Airbrush Thinner. Disassemble the airbrush, then soak the nozzle, needle, and other parts in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 15-30 minutes. Use a cotton swab dipped in thinner to gently clean the airbrush cup and any other accessible parts. Reassemble the airbrush, then run a few bursts of Vallejo Airbrush Thinner through the airbrush to clear any remaining residue. Follow up with a few bursts of water to flush out the system before painting.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Parts
tips.text: Warped kit parts can be repaired by gently warming them with a heat gun, then carefully reshaping them over a flat surface or using tweezers. For best results, use a low-temperature heat gun and apply heat evenly across the part. Once reshaped, allow the part to cool slowly to prevent warping again. For large parts, consider using a small vice with soft jaws to hold the part flat while cooling.
